learning_outcomes.text: Upon completion of the course, the student will be able to model, simulate, and analyze the performance of production systems using Petri nets (particularly non-autonomous and colored) and the software Witness. They will be able to interpret simulation results, identify bottlenecks, and propose concrete improvements to optimize the system's operation.
Understand the fundamental principles of Petri nets and their extensions (synchronized, timed, interpreted, stochastic, colored).
Gain knowledge of discrete event systems and simulation methods for production systems.
Getting to grips with Witness software.
Be able to model discrete event and production systems using Petri nets adapted to industrial realities.
Conduct simulations using specialized tools such as Witness and PIPE and interpret the obtained results.
Perform a critical analysis of the performance of modeled systems to identify and implement improvement strategies.
Be aware of the challenges related to performance optimization in production environments.
Develop a rigorous and critical approach to operational decision-making.
Prepare to apply these skills in a professional context, emphasizing quality and process efficiency.

syllabus_topics: Definition and importance of Petri nets
Applications in production systems
Non-Autonomous Petri Nets: Concepts and general properties
Synchronized Petri nets: principles and applications
Timed Petri nets: time management and modeling
Interpreted Petri nets: event interpretation
Stochastic Petri nets: probability integration
Definition and advantages of Colored Petri Nets
Application examples of Colored Petri Nets in production systems
Solving exercises on non-autonomous Petri nets (modeling and analysis)
Solving exercises on colored Petri nets (application to complex systems)
Introduction to discrete simulation
Objectives and applications of simulation
The simulation process
Modeling approaches
Introduction to Witness
Basic modeling elements
Basic routing laws
Illustrative example of Witness
Taking ranges into account
Variables, Attributes and Resources
Other routing laws
Permanent and temporary assembly
Production machines and multi-cycle machines
Illustrative example of advanced analysis and optimization
Creating a production model with concepts of passive and active items, machines and inventories
Configuration of basic parameters
Run and analyze results
Introduction to model validation, highlighting flows, capacities and bottlenecks
Integrate the notion of production ranges and analyze their contribution to improving item routing
Integrate resources and understand the differences between activity resources and process resources
Integrate the concepts of assembly machines, production machines and multi-cycle machines, and understand the differences between machine types
Execute and analyze results for each type of integrated element
Select the case study to be modeled by drawing lots from a portfolio of case studies
Create the model using Witness advanced features
Analysis of results and suggestions for improvement
teaching_methods: Interactive lectures with visual aids and case studies
Tutorials (TD) in the form of practical exercises
Practical sessions (TP) involving the use of specialized tools (such as Witness and PIPE)
